analysis.title: Europe Open - Next phase
key_insights: USD retains post-midterm losses and USTs are higher, with US 10-year yields at 4.845%. Nasdaq futures are weak again, Kospi fell as much as 5.28% overnight, and China/HK stocks outperformed (Hang Seng +3.55%).

Brent is trading at $94 after a near 9% oil selloff. The initial move came from VP Vance's comments linking the Democratic midterm win to voter frustration over the Iran war. Citi Research says the Democratic win added to US-Iran dealmaking momentum, but re-escalation risk remains.

Citi's oil base case (60% probability) is gradual US/Iran de-escalation before year-end and into next year, with Brent declining toward $70/bbl in 2027. The bull case (30%) has Brent back at $120. The USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier is due in the Middle East by end of November, which could bring a lull and then renewed escalation risk.

BoE decides at 12:00 GMT. Citi expects a 25bp hike in Bank Rate to 4.0%, most likely on a 7-2 vote (6-3 possible). The MPC may push back against market pricing, and Citi sees a second hike likely in Feb 2027.

Citi's US Rates Strategy says the Q4 refunding gave no long-end support. Treasury kept nominal coupon sizes unchanged but revised guidance to allow an increase in late 2027 (Citi base case is February). Citi expects 20y and 30y sizes to stay unchanged when Treasury eventually raises sizes.
The BoJ September minutes showed policymakers agreed further rate hikes were needed, which reinforces expectations of a December hike. Antipodean bonds and JGBs rallied on lower energy prices.

Citi's US Equity Strategy team does not expect a 'coast is clear' signal after the midterms and says it is premature to assume policy regimes lead to stronger S&P 500 fundamentals. Oil prices and AI sentiment will determine whether a year-end rally occurs.

Citi FX Strategy advises caution in taking signals from post-midterm moves. It still wants to fade USD weakness, especially against EUR, and looks to re-engage an EURNOK downside trade after taking profit yesterday.

FX flows: the eTrading desk saw USD buying by real money overnight. Leveraged accounts bought JPY, NZD and CAD against EUR, CNH and HKD. G10 volumes were 3% below 30-day averages and G10 vols are mostly softer. The options desk sees fresh interest in lower USD gamma trades.
Sweden's October CPIF was flat m/m and 1.1% y/y (from 1.5%), with ex-energy at 0.1%. Citi calls it dovish and expects only one more Riksbank hike, in early 2027.
Norges Bank decides at 09:00 GMT. Consensus is for a hold with 1bp priced. Citi's STIRT desk does not expect a December hike, and sees an unfavorable risk-reward in the 9.25bp priced for that step.

EM calendar: CNB is expected to hike 25bp to 4% (Czech). Banxico is expected to hold at 6.50% with dovish risks to the statement. Copom held rates and Citi expects it to stay on hold. BNM held in line with Citi's expectation.
Gold is up a further 1.3% overnight and retains its gains.

Core inflation is back above 3%, and Citi economists expect the CNB to hike.
